title: 'F1 = 1.0000 across six languages' compares the engine against a near-copy of itself
evidence: README.md:60 and docs/overview.md:102-111 claim F1 = 1.0000. The ground truth is Oracle 1 alone, a keyword regex (ruthless_verify.py:61-100). The cross-validation described at :299 is never implemented (:303). The tool side is simple class names regex-parsed from PlantUML, stored in a dict keyed by simple name (:95, :225-234). The engine finds classes with the same keyword-plus-identifier heuristic (pass1_discovery.rs:249-349). 184 of the engine's 188 denylisted names (class_diagram.rs:163, 346-537) also appear in ruthless_config.json:59-92, which is applied to both sides (ruthless_verify.py:88, 232). Examples: Configuration, Root, Table, Logger, HomeScreen.
impact: The metric cannot detect wrong packages, nesting errors, duplicate simple names, or any error in the semantic phases. A real class named Configuration or Logger is removed from both truth and output, so recall is 1.0 by construction. The number cannot be falsified and will not survive external review.
recommendation: Withdraw the claim until it is re-measured. Score fully-qualified declarations against javac with SemanticDB, and against compiler-backed SCIP indexers for other languages, on pinned corpora with bootstrap CIs (suites S3, S13). Move the oracles into a separately reviewed package that is not allowed to share lists, filters or heuristics with the engine.

title: Field-type TH_USES edges are treated as supertypes, so nearly every class with a field is reported as Decorator and Composite
evidence: Pass 5 adds a TH_USES edge from each class to every field type, primitives included (`builder.symbol(0xB000_0005)` is None, so `.unwrap_or(SK_EXTERNAL)`). decorator.rs and composite.rs take all `th_edges` with `from_sym == sym_id`, with no relation filter, then test `parent_types.contains(&f.type_id)`, which holds for any typed field: Decorator 85, Composite 75. facade.rs counts fields with `type_id != u32::MAX`; primitive ids qualify, so three ints earn Facade 70. A Python re-implementation over examples/test_patterns_codebase gives 37 reports on 13 of 35 classes, and only 9 name a real participant (precision ≈0.24). The Facade and Adapter samples display <<Decorator>>, which is checked first.
impact: Pattern stereotypes drawn on class diagrams are wrong for most classes of a real codebase, and pattern counts and the visitor's pattern_frequency metric are dominated by noise.
recommendation: Build a supertype index restricted to TH_EXTENDS/TH_IMPLEMENTS once and use it in every rule; exclude primitives, stubs and external types from structural predicates. Require call-graph evidence for Decorator/Composite/Adapter: an overriding method that forwards to the wrapped field, and for Composite a loop over a collection of the component type. Add negative fixtures (POJO, DTO with three ints, linked-list Node) asserting no pattern, and gate per-pattern precision in CI.

title: Declaration names come from token-window heuristics and are wrong for annotated members, every parameter and long class headers
evidence: Methods take the last identifier before the first '(' (pass1:696-745), and fields the last before the first '=' (748-791). Parameters fall through to the first identifier (793-889). The class keyword must appear within 15 tokens (645). The Annotation skip (703) never fires, because annotations are never leaf tokens (ingestion java.rs:69-70). A re-implementation (scratchpad sim_pass1.py) gives `@GetMapping("/x") ... getUser(` → GetMapping; `@GeneratedValue(strategy=..) Long id` → strategy; parameter `String name` → String; `final Long id` → final; `@Entity @Table(..) class User` → Entity; `@Import({A.class,B.class}) class Cfg` → B. A Spring/Lombok blocklist is hardcoded at 865-883.
impact: In Spring, JPA and JUnit 5 code, members and classes are named after annotations, and every parameter takes its first token's text as its name. Call graph, UML, traceability and resolution inherit these names, and the downstream 'Entity' blocklist hides real classes.
recommendation: Extract names structurally. In Phase 2, record in a side array the token of each declaration's tree-sitter `name` field (type declarations, methods, constructors), plus each variable_declarator and formal_parameter name; Pass 1 reads it. Emit one SK_FIELD or SK_LOCAL_VAR per declarator: java.rs:42 currently emits the declaration and its declarators, and `int a, b;` yields one field named b. Delete the hardcoded name lists. Done when golden name tests pass on Spring PetClinic and a JPA entity fixture.

title: State, object, component, deployment, composite, use-case and activity views ignore UMA data and invent content
evidence: State machines always show "Uninitialized" and "Active" states with "entry / onInit()", "do / executeWork()" and "exit / cleanup()", and never read `sm.states`. Object diagrams draw one object per class with "references" edges between consecutive classes, while `uma.objects` (allocation sites) goes unused. Components get an invented `I{name}` interface, deployments get "art_X.jar" nodes, and composites get `port in_port/out_port`. Use-case actors are classes whose names end in "Service" or "App". JSON activities chain nodes in a line and ignore `act.edges`. Every Mermaid gantt task is `0, 1s`.
impact: Most behavioral and deployment views look plausible but contain no program facts. They mislead reviewers and make the "14 UML 2.5 diagrams" claim impossible to verify.
recommendation: Render only modeled facts: states and transitions with guards from StateRecord/TransitionRecord, objects from ObjectRecord plus points-to links, component interfaces from provided/required sets, activity flow from ActivityEdge, and sequence fragments from CombinedFragment. When a diagram has no evidence, emit an explicit "no data" note instead of a placeholder. Note that UMA's own state model is a 2-state placeholder, which is another auditor's area. Done means golden fixtures whose every element traces back to a source span.

title: JSON Graph IR fabricates source provenance and 'verified' metadata
evidence: Class nodes get `file: Some(format!("{}.java", name))` and `lines: vec![1, 5, 10]`. Sequence, state and object nodes get `"{name}.java"` with line 1. The composite root is "OpenHeartEngine.java" for every input. Each GraphIR carries the constants `compiler_hash: "0x83D2D2B2"` and `verified: true`. Meanwhile every ClassRecord has `uml_link` holding the real file, line and column, and the web editor navigates by `nodeData?.file`. The shipped class.json assigns TypeScript interfaces and Python classes to `.java` files.
impact: Click-to-source opens files that do not exist or the wrong lines, which contradicts the 'O(1) bidirectional traceability' headline. The 'verified' flag is meaningless.
recommendation: Fill file and range from `class_rec.uml_link` or TRA sym_span, taking the path from tca.file_records, and emit null when unknown. Set compiler_hash to the real snapshot digest. Either drop `verified` or compute it from real checks (unique ids, all edge endpoints resolve). Add a JSON Schema for GraphIR and validate against it in CI. Done means every node with a span maps back to its declaring token range.

title: Phase 9 has no working extractor for six diagram types: the state machine is a fixed template, four extractors are empty, and the object extractor misreads AST ids
evidence: StateMachineExtractor ignores `_ssa` and emits, for every class, states {0 initial, 1 final} plus one 0→1 transition per method. The composite, communication, interaction-overview and timing extractors have empty bodies and return (); behavioral/mod.rs:48-50 calls them for no output. ObjectDiagramExtractor calls `sta.symbol(ssa_rec.orig_sym_id)`, but SSA's orig_sym_id is an AST node index (`let sym_id = node;`), so objects are arbitrary symbol hits, and it stores ssa_id as label_text_id. No exporter reads `uma.objects`; objects and label_texts are never serialized. The paper and ROADMAP claim IFDS type-state state machines and thread-analysis timing.
impact: Object, composite-structure, state-machine, communication, interaction-overview and timing diagrams have no analysis behind them (deployment, use case and profile have no extractor at all), so the paper's tab:uml and the 14-diagram claim are not backed by code.
recommendation: Implement real extractors or drop the types. Object diagrams: Andersen allocation sites plus field points-to links (Tonella and Potrich, Reverse Engineering of Object Oriented Code, 2005). State machines: enum- or int-typed state fields with guarded assignments via SSA, CDG and ROBDD guards (Sen and Mall, SoSyM 2016), emitting nothing when no state variable exists. Communication diagrams: sequence records plus object naming (Rountev and Connell, ICSE 2005). Persist ObjectRecords and labels in .uma, and correct the paper and ROADMAP.

title: Pattern rules are name and keyword heuristics that miss canonical GoF instances and flag unrelated classes
evidence: Singleton scores 100 for any field named 'instance' or typed as its own class, so `class Node { Node next; }` is a Singleton. It has no static or constructor checks and rejects enums. Factory means the name contains 'factory'. State means it contains 'state' or 'strategy' (IfStatement, RealEstate, every *Strategy). Observer needs add/register/attach plus 'listener', so the repo's own NewsAgency.attach(Observer) is missed. Template Method needs a protected method, so DataMiner is missed, and Logistics (Factory Method) is missed too: recall 6/9 on the repo's corpus. `has_private_constructor` scans SK_METHOD only, while constructors are SK_CONSTRUCTOR. The structural Singleton in src/symbol/uml_meta/patterns.rs is never called.
impact: Detection follows identifier spelling rather than design: renaming a class flips the result, textbook Observer/Factory Method/Template Method and enum, holder or Kotlin-object Singletons go undetected, and recursive data types become Singletons.
recommendation: Re-specify each pattern as structural plus behavioral constraints in the style of PINOT (Shi and Olsson, ASE 2006). Singleton: private constructors, a static self-typed field and a static accessor that assigns it (CFG/SSA), plus enum, holder and Kotlin `object` variants. Observer: a collection of an interface type and a loop invoking its method. Factory Method: an overridden method returning an abstract type that allocates a concrete subtype. Template Method: a concrete method calling abstract hooks (CGA). Use names only as a weak prior; revive or delete the dead detector.

title: Class extractor silently drops legitimate user types through a 188-name blacklist and lexical filters
evidence: `is_reserved_keyword` rejects user classes named Context, Singleton, Logger, Root, Entity, Configuration, Table, Value, Error, Update, List or Thread, plus project-specific names (HomeScreen, INVESTOR, OpenHeart). Context and Singleton are canonical GoF participant names, and src/uma/mod.rs:70 runs detection only over extracted classes, so the textbook Singleton is never examined. The repo's own examples/huge_enterprise_src/.../core/Entity.java interface is dropped. Names with `$` or non-ASCII letters, *Binding names and lowercase names are rejected. Test exclusion matches only '/src/test/', while ingestion stores raw OS paths, so on Windows test classes are kept.
impact: Class diagrams, pattern detection and every derived diagram omit real types without warning, and output differs between Linux and Windows.
recommendation: Delete the blacklist and fix the misclassifications it hides at their source in Phases 1-3 (annotations, constants or framework names emitted as SK_CLASS). Filter only on symbol kind and origin (synthetic, external, generated), accept full JLS and Kotlin identifiers, normalize paths before test detection, and make test inclusion a CLI flag. Add regression fixtures declaring Context, Singleton, Entity, Root and a Unicode-named class.

title: Sequence diagrams list messages in the wrong order with no nesting, returns or fragments, and all scenarios merge into one diagram
evidence: Callers are expanded from a LIFO stack after all of a method's calls are emitted, so for A→B, A→C the sub-calls of C print before those of B, and each method is expanded once, wherever it is popped. `combined_fragments` is always empty, although `_cfa` is passed and docs/uml_derivation.md:89 promises ROBDD-derived alt/loop/opt. There is no depth bound or library filter. PlantUML emits activate/return/deactivate right after each call, so activations never nest. The actor is declared `act_Actor` but its messages come from `part_Actor`, creating a phantom participant. Every entry-point scenario is concatenated into one diagram.
impact: Sequence diagrams misstate call order and nesting, the core semantics of the notation, and become unreadable walls of messages on any non-trivial project.
recommendation: Emit one diagram per scenario by ordered, depth-bounded inlining of call sites in CFG order (Rountev, Volgin and Reddoch, PASTE 2005). Map branch and loop regions to alt/opt/loop/break fragments with guards, emit replies and nested activations, and mark async calls (Thread.start, Executor.submit, CompletableFuture). Name lifelines by receiver object via points-to (Rountev and Connell, ICSE 2005), and choose entry points from framework semantics (main, @RequestMapping, JUnit, Android lifecycle).

title: Class diagrams lose multiplicity, collection element types, relationship kinds and member signatures, and collide on simple names
evidence: `is_collection: 0` is hard-coded. Type refs resolve from their first token, so `List<Observer>` becomes List and the one-to-many link to Observer vanishes. Phase 3's `sta.associations` (AssocKind, multiplicity, role names) is never read. Return types are recorded as associations (they are dependencies), while parameters, locals and `new` yield nothing. With multiple interface extends only the last survives. Member modifiers are cast `as u8`, losing default/sealed/varargs bits. Exporters treat composition as 'final field', draw nesting as `*--` (Mermaid), omit parameters and key classes by simple name, so nested Builders merge. PlantUML keeps one edge per pair; XMI emits only `Class_{id}`.
impact: Diagrams omit the relationships reviewers need most (one-to-many, ownership, usage), misrender overloads, generics and same-named types, and cannot round-trip to UML tools.
recommendation: Model type arguments in Phase 3 (a TypeRef tree), consume sta.associations, and classify relationships per Guéhéneuc and Albin-Amiot (OOPSLA 2004): association, aggregation or composition by exclusivity and lifetime, with multiplicity from collection or array types. Add «use»/«create» dependencies. Key elements by qualified name, and emit operation signatures, UML templates, {static}/{abstract} and enumeration literals. Export OMG XMI 2.5.1, validated against UML 2.5.1 and import-tested in Papyrus, Enterprise Architect and Visual Paradigm, to reach IntelliJ/ObjectAid-level fidelity.

title: Quadratic and cubic scans in sequence, class, component and pattern extraction create performance cliffs on large codebases
evidence: For each entry point the extractor rebuilds a HashMap of all `site_to_edge_map` entries, and for each visited method it scans every `cga.call_sites` entry: O(entries × reachable × sites) time, with unbounded memory and no depth limit. Each class scans all `sta.th_edges` and runs `tra.uml_links.iter().find`, giving O(C·E + C·L). Four pattern rules repeat the full th_edges scan per class. Component extraction re-runs package extraction and scans all th_edges per package. One info-level log line is written per class candidate.
impact: At 1M LOC (about 50K classes, 500K TH edges, thousands of entry points) these loops reach roughly 10^10 or more iterations, so Phase 9 runs for hours or exhausts memory instead of scaling.
recommendation: Build CSR indexes once (supertypes by from_sym, call sites by caller, uml_links by sym_id). Bound the sequence builder by depth and size, memoize per-method message summaries, and parallelize per class and per entry point (rayon). Add criterion benchmarks on Spring Framework, Apache Commons and JHotDraw with time and peak-RSS budgets enforced in CI.

title: The .uma reader misparses the design-pattern table and desynchronizes on large records; objects and labels are never persisted
evidence: The writer emits each pattern as class_sym u32, `pattern_kind as u32`, `confidence as u32` and reserved u32 (16 bytes). The reader consumes u32+u16+u16+u32 (12 bytes): confidence always reads 0, every later record is misaligned, and there is no end-offset check. Counts are written `as u16` while all records follow, so above 65,535 messages or blocks the reader desynchronizes, unchecked `bytes[offset..]` slicing panics, and `with_capacity` trusts header counts. Objects and label_texts are never written. Artifact inspection prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID'; the round-trip test compares only version and hash.
impact: Every consumer of a persisted .uma reads corrupted pattern data, and large projects can crash the reader, so the artifact is not a faithful interchange format.
recommendation: Define the layout once with derive-based codecs (binrw or zerocopy) or a schema (FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto), and use u32 counts. Make reads bounds-checked and error-returning, assert the payload ends exactly at the CRC, add sections for objects and labels, and add a proptest asserting read(write(x)) == x for every record type.

title: Silent narrowing casts cap the system at 65,535 files, 65,535 columns, 64 KB tokens, 256 blocks/method and 65,535-member SCCs
evidence: Narrowing casts: `file_id as u16`, header file_count `len() as u16`, `col: start.column as u16` (wraps), token len `.min(u16::MAX)` (truncates the text), `def_block: (def_block & 0xFF) as u8`, `raw_members.len() as u16`. The 24-bit line limit is only a debug_assert, and overflow-checks are off. In a minified .js (the server collects .js) wider than 65,535 columns, tokens at col c and c+65,536 share a sort_key, and finalize aborts the run with 'Invariant 2 Violation'. Consumers index the sorted token_records by token_id, so any reordering silently corrupts lookups.
impact: Repositories the size of the JDK, or containing a single minified bundle, fail Phase 1. Methods with more than 256 blocks map SSA definitions and traceability to the wrong block; feasibility.rs even documents the truncation.
recommendation: Key tokens by (file_id: u32, byte_offset: u32) and keep a per-file line-start table for line/column, as rustc's SourceMap or the line-index crate do. Widen def_block, member_count and the file counts to u32. Replace `as` casts with `try_from(...)?` and typed errors, and enable overflow-checks in CI builds. Add tests with 70K synthetic files, a 200K-column line and a 300-block method.

title: Secondary token sweep fabricates classes and fields in pure Java and misplaces Kotlin members
evidence: The sweep runs for every language. Java `var` locals and identifiers named `val` create public SK_FIELDs on current_class_sym (414-453), which is never reset at class end or file change (257). Class literals, or variables named record or object, followed by a capitalized identifier create phantom SK_CLASS/SK_RECORD symbols in the root scope (396-407). On one Java test, sim_pass1.py produced TestConfig, ErrorCode and Mode plus fields order, result and compute. Only the first (file, name) pair gets a symbol (433). Kotlin depends entirely on this sweep: its AST falls back to the JS grammar (registry.rs:19-28), and ingestion uses the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:29-30).
impact: Java output gains fake classes and fields, and because they sit in the global root scope, any file's lookups can capture them. Kotlin members attach to the wrong class and never get types. Downstream ALL_CAPS filters only mask the problem.
recommendation: Disable the sweep for languages that have an AST adapter. Give Kotlin a real front end: the tree-sitter-kotlin grammar (fwcd) plus a KotlinSemanticAdapter covering primary-constructor properties, companion objects, extension receivers, top-level file facades, nullable types and typealiases. Alternatively ingest semanticdb-kotlinc output. Add a regression test asserting that Java fixtures produce no symbols without a decl_node other than externals and packages.

title: Containment tree corrupted: append_child re-links already-chained symbols and orphans are parented to the first file's module
evidence: append_child never unlinks a child from its previous sibling chain (builder.rs:83-96). Pass 1 re-appends top-level classes to their package while they stay in the module's chain (579-620). The safety sweep then parents every orphan, including the modules of files 2..N and the root packages, under symbol 0, the first file's module, to satisfy Invariant 2 (623-628). sim_chain.py on package com.a with File1 {A, B} and File2 {C} yields children(com.a) = [A, B, Module(File2), com]: C is lost, its own parent package appears as a child, and com's parent is Module(File1).
impact: Package class and subpackage counts, component interface counts and the pattern detectors' member lists are wrong even for a two-file project. The package tree is rooted under an arbitrary file's module.
recommendation: Treat parent_sym as the only source of truth. Finish all reparenting, then derive children once as CSR sorted by (parent, declaration order), and rebuild or drop first_child/next_sibling. Add a synthetic project root and real package roots instead of symbol 0. Turn Invariant 2 into a check that chains are acyclic and agree with parent_sym. Add multi-file, multi-package fixtures that assert exact child lists.

title: Type hierarchy comes from token scans: type arguments, bounds and Kotlin property types become supertypes
evidence: Phase 2 drops generic_type, so the AST path (40-74) misses `extends Base<T>`. The token path (76-157) treats every identifier after extends, implements or ':' up to '{' or ';' as a supertype. sim_pass5.py: `class OrderService extends BaseService<Order,OrderRepository> implements Auditable<User>` gives EXTENDS BaseService, Order and User, and class_diagram.rs:283-288 then reports User as the superclass. `class Repo<T extends BaseEntity>` gives EXTENDS BaseEntity. Kotlin `data class Invoice(val customer: Customer..)` gives EXTENDS Customer and scans on into the next declaration. Cross-file interfaces get TH_EXTENDS edges to SK_EXTERNALs (60-68), and interface-to-interface becomes TH_IMPLEMENTS (141-146).
impact: Generalization is wrong for generic base classes (Spring Data, generic services and DAOs) and for most Kotlin data classes. CHA dispatch follows the spurious edges, and sanitize_th_graph may delete correct edges to break the resulting cycles.
recommendation: Read supertypes only from tree-sitter fields: superclass, interfaces, extends_interfaces, permits, and Kotlin delegation_specifiers. Resolve the head of each generic_type and keep type arguments separately. Allow at most one superclass per class, and choose the relation from both declaration kinds (JLS 8.1.4, 8.1.5, 9.1.3). Store the superclass explicitly, delete the token path, and report cycles as diagnostics instead of deleting edges.

title: Declaration coverage gaps: enum constants, anonymous classes, records, interface constants, and catch/resource/for-each/pattern variables
evidence: The Java adapter has no arm for enum_constant, constant_declaration, annotation_type_body, catch_formal_parameter, resource_specification, inferred_parameters, compact_constructor_declaration or constructor_body, so all of them hit Drop with their subtrees. SK_ENUM_CONSTANT and SK_ANON_CLASS are never constructed, yet class_diagram.rs:209 and tra/builder.rs:84 consume them. Anonymous-class methods become children of the enclosing local-variable or method symbol. Record components become SK_PARAMs with no implicit fields or accessors (JLS 8.10.3), and for-each and pattern variables get no symbol at all.
impact: Enums render without literals, and anonymous listeners and strategies are invisible to CHA and pattern detection. Records have no attributes. Constructor bodies, which carry dependency-injection wiring, never reach Phase 4 to 6 or the composition check.
recommendation: Write a JLS declaration-kind coverage test with one fixture per kind, then add adapter arms and symbols for each. Create SK_ANON_CLASS with a TH edge to the instantiated type. Synthesize implicit members: record fields, accessors and canonical constructor (JLS 8.10.3), and enum values/valueOf (8.9.3). Scope catch, resource, for-each and pattern variables to their construct.

title: Pattern output has no roles, participants, calibrated confidence or conflict resolution, and covers 11 of 23 GoF patterns
evidence: DesignPatternRecord holds only {class_sym, pattern_kind, confidence}: no instance id and no role→class map (Context, Strategy, ConcreteStrategy). ClassRecord.design_pattern is one u8 set by the first match, so rule order picks the stereotype. Confidences are uncalibrated constants (100/95/90/85/80/75/70). Mutually exclusive kinds both fire: PaymentStrategy gets State 85 and Strategy 95, and State is displayed. Visitor, Command, Proxy, Iterator, Mediator, Chain of Responsibility, Abstract Factory, Bridge, Flyweight, Memento, Prototype and Interpreter are absent. chain.rs re-implements detect_all as a second pipeline.
impact: Output cannot be scored against role-level benchmarks (P-MARt, DPB), cannot explain a match, and cannot tell Strategy from State or Decorator from Proxy.
recommendation: Introduce PatternInstance {pattern, roles: Map<Role, Vec<SymId>>, evidence: Vec<Fact>, score} and serialize it. Match with similarity scoring over relation matrices (Tsantalis et al., TSE 2006) or explanation-based constraint solving (DeMIMA, Guéhéneuc and Antoniol, TSE 2008). Calibrate scores (isotonic or Platt) on labeled data, and disambiguate (State if the context reassigns its delegate internally, otherwise Strategy). Cover all 23 GoF patterns and keep a single pipeline; consider DPDf-style learned features as a ranking layer.

title: Binary artifact readers panic or allocate huge buffers on malformed input
evidence: There are 291 .unwrap() calls in src, 286 outside tests, and 208 are bytes[a..b].try_into().unwrap(). 84% of the non-test ones are in five serializers: uma 96, symbol 66, tra 46, ast 17, psa 15. uma/serializer.rs:268-300 loops over counts taken from the header and slices bytes[offset..offset+4] without checking the remaining length. Before that it calls Vec::with_capacity(class_count) with a count read from the file. The CRC-64 check (239-249) catches accidental corruption, not crafted files.
impact: inspect and every artifact reader crash on truncated or hostile files, either from an out-of-bounds index or a multi-GB allocation.
recommendation: Add a bounds-checked cursor (read_u32()? returning InvalidData). Cap counts by the remaining bytes before allocating. Replace unwrap with ?. Add a cargo-fuzz target for each reader.

title: Overflow checks are off in dev and test builds, alongside 846 unchecked numeric casts
evidence: Cargo.toml:23 sets overflow-checks = false under [profile.dev]. The test profile inherits from dev, so cargo test cannot catch integer overflow. src contains 846 numeric 'as' casts (pass1_discovery.rs 54, uma/serializer.rs 40, pass5_hierarchy.rs 27, cfg/builder/mod.rs 26). Example: uma/serializer.rs:39-42 writes counts as len() as u16, which silently truncates above 65,535.
impact: On large repositories, silent wraparound and truncation produce wrong graphs or corrupt artifacts while the tests still pass.
recommendation: Remove overflow-checks = false and keep opt-level = 2. Use u16::try_from(..)? and checked arithmetic in serializers and index math. Enable clippy::cast_possible_truncation.

title: 'O(1) bidirectional traceability' is not delivered: forward and navigation queries are scans
evidence: forward_sym_query walks backward from the partition point and breaks only when the file changes (sym_span.rs:60-70). That costs O(log N + symbols before the token in the file), not the documented O(log N + k). forward_cs_query never stops once first_token_id < token_id (cs_span.rs:51-60). UMLLinks are 'sorted for O(1) array index access', but they cover only UML kinds, so they cannot be indexed by sym_id. NavigationEngine::to_source does a linear .find and from_source a full filter, and class diagrams run a .find per class (O(C*U)).
impact: Query latency grows with file and repository size, and the README's headline O(1) traceability claim is false for every forward and navigation query.
recommendation: Exploit span nesting: store each span's enclosing-span index (or reuse the BP AST's parent/LCA), binary-search the innermost span, then walk parents for O(log N + k). Use an interval tree such as rust-lapper for non-nested data. Give UMLLinks a dense sym_id-to-slot array, break cs queries early, and add CSR offset tables for blocks and SSA. Done means criterion p50/p99 latency benchmarks at 1M symbols.

title: Activity diagrams discard CFG guards, exception edges, loops and labels; the label extractor reads the wrong token
evidence: Every edge becomes EDGE_KIND_CONTROL with guard_text_id 0, although the CFG labels edges True/False/Except/Switch/LoopBack. loop_depth is always 0 despite `cfg.loop_info`; swimlane_count and end_node_count are hard-coded to 1; switch blocks with more than two successors become ACTION; FORK/JOIN/EXCEPTION nodes are never produced. The label is computed then discarded (`_label_text`; label_text_id = block_id). LabelExtractor treats `bpa.node_attr` (packed visibility/modifier/operator bits) as a token index, so plain statements read token #0. Its byte slice at max_chars-3 can panic mid-character on long non-ASCII tokens (latent). Exporters show only the first 6-8 functions, as 'Block_N' rectangles.
impact: Activity diagrams are unlabeled block graphs without decision guards or exception paths, short of the decision/merge semantics the paper claims.
recommendation: Map edge types to guards ([cond]/[else], case labels) using the branch condition's TRA token span, and render exception edges as UML exception handlers or interruptible regions. Emit explicit decision/merge nodes, fork/join for thread and async starts, and partitions for inlined callees. Build labels from statement token spans, truncate on char boundaries (`char_indices`), store them in label_texts, and render each node kind with its UML shape.

title: Phase 9 output is nondeterministic across runs because HashSet/HashMap iteration order leaks into records
evidence: `implements_syms` and `association_syms` come from `HashSet::into_iter()`, and sequence lifelines from `HashMap::into_values()`. Both use std's randomly seeded RandomState, so element order varies per process. That order is serialized into .uma (changing its CRC) and drives exporter edge and participant order, despite CHANGELOG 'Deterministic generation for all 14'.
impact: Identical inputs yield different .uma bytes and diagram layouts, defeating reproducible builds, hash-chain caching, golden-file tests and diagram diffs.
recommendation: Use BTreeSet/BTreeMap or sort before emission (by symbol id or qualified name). Add a test that runs Phase 9 twice on the same input and compares bytes, and audit the exporters for the same HashMap ordering.

title: Artifact deserializers slice fixed header offsets after only a minimal length check, panicking on truncated-but-magic-valid files
evidence: `inspect` dispatches on magic then calls sub-deserializers. Readers validate only a coarse minimum length (e.g. `bytes.len() < UMA_HEADER_SIZE + 8`, uma/serializer.rs:230) or `buf.len() < 96` (tra:114) and then index many fixed ranges via `try_into().unwrap()` and derive counts used to slice payloads. A file with a valid magic/CRC-consistent prefix but a truncated or oversized declared count can panic on slice-out-of-range during body parsing. No `catch_unwind` guards these.
impact: `openheart inspect` on a crafted or corrupted artifact can panic instead of returning the intended 'corrupted artifact' error; the same parsers are reachable from the engine open path.
recommendation: Bounds-check every read against remaining length and return `io::Error` on shortfall (consider a small cursor helper or the `zerocopy`/`bytes` crates). Validate declared element counts against remaining bytes before allocating/slicing. Add fuzz targets (cargo-fuzz) for each `.tca/.bpa/.sta/.cfa/.ssa/.cga/.tra/.psa/.uma/.scpg` reader.

title: Semantics-based design-pattern and architecture recovery
evidence: Singleton fires on any field named 'instance' or 'getinstance', typed as the class itself, or named like the class, and scores it 100 (src/uma/patterns/singleton.rs:20-31). Observer fires on any method that starts with add/register/attach and contains 'listener', scores it 85, and never uses the call graph (src/uma/patterns/observer.rs:11,25-38).
impact: A linked-list Node with a `Node next` field becomes a Singleton at 100% confidence, and renamed variants are missed. Pattern recovery is a differentiator only if it is accurate and measured.
recommendation: Match structural and behavioural signatures: private constructors, static accessors that return the class's own type, role-consistent call-graph and points-to facts, and field accesses. Output participant roles with calibrated confidences. Evaluate on P-MARt and DPB, and publish precision and recall per pattern.

title: Very long functions hold most of the risk
evidence: Of 834 non-test functions (lengths by brace matching), the median is 10 lines and p90 is 65. 118 are over 50 lines, 43 over 100 and 13 over 200. Largest: pass1_discovery.rs:18-633 run (616), uma/serializer.rs:229-679 read (451), server.rs:366-762 process_analyze_request (397), class_diagram.rs:13-344 extract (332), json.rs:121-421 (301), main.rs:101-345 cmd_analyze (245).
impact: These functions cannot be unit-tested, and defects such as the silent repo fallback hide inside 400-line handlers.
recommendation: Split by concern: routing, validation, phase orchestration, record codecs. Enforce clippy::too_many_lines and cognitive_complexity limits in CI.

title: Class-diagram detail falls far short of UML reverse-engineering tools
evidence: Methods print as `name() : Ret` with no parameters (UMA stores only param_count), so overloads show up as identical lines. Each type is reduced to a single symbol name, so generics, arrays and nullability disappear. Static and abstract markers, multiplicities and role names are missing. Composition is inferred from the `final` modifier. JSON marks a field as aggregation whenever its type name contains "List", "Set" or "Array", which catches names like `Settings` and `Listener`. Mermaid prints fields as `+name Type`.
impact: The diagrams lack the detail users expect from IntelliJ UML or Papyrus reverse engineering, and some relationship kinds are wrong.
recommendation: Extend the UMA model and the IR with full signatures (parameter names and types, type arguments, array and nullable flags, modifiers). Render them with PlantUML `{static}`/`{abstract}` and quoted generic labels, and with Mermaid `~T~` generics. Derive aggregation and multiplicity from resolved Collection subtypes, and use composition only for owned lifecycles. Done means fixture parity with a reference generator such as the PlantUML Maven or Gradle plugins.

title: Package, component and deployment views are containment counts with no dependency or build-metadata grounding
evidence: PackageRecord holds only class and subpackage counts, with no inter-package dependencies, although docs/uml_derivation.md:60 promises them. Components are exactly packages and `_cga` is unused. 'Provided' counts interfaces declared in the package, 'required' counts TH edges (duplicates included) to outside interfaces, and exporters render neither (bare boxes). Deployment reuses packages. No build or deployment metadata is read: pom.xml, build.gradle, module-info.java, DI annotations, Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests.
impact: Architecture views carry no information beyond the directory tree, whereas Structure101, jQAssistant/ArchUnit-based views or Enterprise Architect show dependency structure, cycles and layering.
recommendation: Compute package dependency edges from type references and call edges, with cycle detection (Tarjan SCC) and Martin's metrics (Ca, Ce, I, A, D). Derive components from Maven/Gradle modules, JPMS modules and Spring @Component/@Service beans, with implemented interfaces as provided and injected interface-typed fields as required. Derive deployment from Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes or Helm manifests, and mark it unavailable when they are absent.

title: sat_count silently saturates at u64::MAX, and consumers then wrap
evidence: Counts above 2^64 return u64::MAX through saturating operations (sat_count.rs:60,79,90,92), with no flag marking the result as inexact. Phase 9 sums them with a plain `+=` (uma/visitor.rs:214), which wraps because overflow-checks=false. PathMetrics serializes `mean = sat_count as f32`, which is not a mean, and from_bytes drops unwind_depth.
impact: Functions with 64 or more independent decisions, common in generated code, get clamped counts, and the aggregate totals wrap to small nonsense values.
recommendation: Count with num-bigint BigUint, as biodivine-lib-bdd's exact_cardinality and CUDD's Cudd_ApaCountMinterm do, and store a log2 f64 plus an exactness bit in the 16-byte record. Use checked adds in consumers. Done means a test with 80 sequential branches reporting exactly 2^80.
